benchmark_name: M3Exam: A Multilingual, Multimodal, Multilevel Benchmark for Examining Large Language Models (M3Exam)
humanities_role_explanation: Items are real school exam questions across subjects (language, math, social science, natural science) used to test general intelligence; humanities material (language, history, social studies) supplies some items but the benchmark does not target humanities disciplinary competence.
benchmark_modalities_explanation: Text multiple-choice questions in 9 languages; about 23% (2,816) require images, which are clipped and placed via placeholders. Multimodal evaluation was run on English questions only.
analytical_tasks_explanation: Multiple-choice exam questions from primary, middle and high school graduation exams, covering language, math, social science and natural science. Questions demand language understanding, domain knowledge, cultural knowledge and problem solving, and image-based questions test multimodal understanding and cross-image reasoning.

general_purpose_benchmark.note: Broad multi-subject, multilingual, multilevel exam benchmark intended to evaluate general intelligence of LLMs.

evaluates_generative_llm.note: ChatGPT, GPT-4, Claude-instant, BLOOM 176B, Vicuna 13B; multimodal: BLIP-2, InstructBLIP, Fromage, OpenFlamingo; plus Flan-T5.

quantitative_metrics.note: Accuracy, compared against random and passing-score baselines.

published_after_march_2023.note: NeurIPS 2023 Datasets and Benchmarks track; references include works from May 2023.

summary: M3Exam is a benchmark of 12,317 real, official exam questions in 9 languages across three educational levels, with about 23% requiring images. The authors evaluate text-only LLMs and multimodal models, finding that models struggle in low-resource and non-Latin-script languages and with complex images, and that performance does not decrease monotonically with level.
key_findings: GPT-4 is the best model with 72.92% average accuracy, and the only model above 60%. Performance is worst on Javanese (55.26 for GPT-4) and Thai (56.04). Multimodal models score below 50% (BLIP-2 49.06 overall on English image questions), barely above text-only Flan-T5 (48.30). Performance shows no clear monotonic decline with education level. English-translation prompting greatly improves ChatGPT on Thai and Javanese.
facets_explanation: Questions and answers come from official exam papers and their official answer sets collected by native speakers in each country; annotators converted them to a unified format, fixed OCR errors and entered the correct answer, with multiple rounds of quality checks. Data are sourced natively per country rather than translated, to retain culture-specific knowledge. Scoring compares the first letter of the output to a single ground-truth option.
results_explanation: GPT-4 reaches 72.92 average accuracy in Table 2 (zero-shot). Input-representation gap: ChatGPT on Javanese rises from 37.47 (Monolingual) to 50.94 (EN-Translation) in Table 3, i.e. about 13 points; Thai rises from 34.09 to 46.49 (12 points). Asymmetry: the paper states models perform worse on non-Latin and low-resource languages such as Thai and Javanese. No human baseline is given. The evaluation set size is not stated as a single number: the test set is the full dataset minus three held-out questions per subject category per level per language, and the count is not given.

humanities_role.quote: we group the questions for each language into four subject categories, namely language, math, social science, and natural science

dataset_size.quote: At the end of the annotation and quality check, our newly introduced M3Exam dataset contains a total of 12,317 questions.

primary_evaluation_setting.quote: We primarily evaluate various LLMs in zero-shot settings.
we also compare zero-shot and few-shot settings from an empirical standpoint with ChatGPT in Section 4.1.

gold_source.quote: We then engage native speakers from each of the selected countries to collect official exam papers along with their answers at the end of each educational level

gold_beyond_stimulus.quote: even when translating the data into English, the question might still be difficult to answer since it may involve background knowledge of each specific language.

gold_community_dependent.quote: collecting real-world natural data of different languages instead of translating from English data is of great importance, as culture and world knowledge are deeply rooted in authentic data

answer_multiplicity.quote: we take the first alphabetic letter of the model's output as the prediction and compare it with the ground truth answer to calculate the accuracy scores.

reported_format_gap_kind.quote: using the English translations of the questions greatly improves their performance.

reported_best_score.quote: GPT-4 [31] being the only model to achieve over 60% accuracy

reported_cultural_asymmetry.quote: existing models generally perform worse for non-Latin languages, such as Chinese (despite being relatively high-resource), as well as low-resource languages like Javanese
